# Read-back

This is a rowing training session for four rowers (two pairs: A/B and C/D) working on two shared rowing ergometers. The session has no external deadline; it finishes when all the work is done. The two ergs are the binding constraint — only one pair can use them at a time, so the pairs alternate: while A and B row, C and D rest (and vice versa). A coach is present throughout: they brief the crew before anyone touches a machine, call splits during the first piece, run one-on-one technique drills with each rower in sequence (coach and rower on the machine together, so only one rower can drill at a time), and debrief after cooldown. The session flows through warm-ups (A/B first, then C/D ten minutes later), three four-minute pieces per pair (interlocked so C/D's rest is A/B's work and vice versa), then a three-minute coached technique drill for each rower in turn (A, B, C, D), and finally a ten-minute floor cooldown together. The rests between pieces are not explicit timers — they emerge from the handoff of the machines between pairs. The coach's time is carved into briefing, calling splits (20 minutes, spanning the first piece window), drilling, and debriefing; the coach runs the drills in sequence, not in parallel.
